NATA ('plant') token 2 — the Torah's two planters: God (2:8, va-yita … gan, the garden in Eden) and Noach (the vineyard); token 3 will be Abraham's tamarisk [letter fact]. KEREM ('vineyard') — Torah token 1.

THE VINEYARD INSTALLED on the garden's own precedent [decision recorded]: frozen gen_08 encoded 2:8 as 'plant(e4) ∧ Agent(e4, YHWH_Elohim) ∧ Theme(e4, gan)' + 'WORLD += {gan}' — completed plant-verb, persistent object: the class matched exactly; the install chain runs garden / city / ark / altar / VINEYARD — God's planting and man's echo.

THREE DEBUTS IN ONE VERSE: SHATAH ('drink') — the drink-verb's Torah token 1 is Noach's wine (its next eight tokens are Rebecca's WATER at the well, Gen 24); YAYIN ('wine') tokens 1-2 here — tokens 4-7 are Lot's daughters (19:32-35: wine + father + uncovering, the mirror scene; named as career fact only) [letter facts].

VA-YISHKAR ('and he became drunk') — SHAKHAR ('be drunk') token 1 of THREE in the whole Torah (9:21; 43:34 the brothers drinking free at Joseph's table; Deut 32:42 arrows drunk on blood) [rare-class].

VA-YITGAL — GALAH ('uncover') Torah token 1, HITPAEL (reflexive): 'he uncovered HIMSELF' — the shame is self-made before it is seen [letter fact]; the verb re-converges with the nakedness-noun in Leviticus 18's legalot ervah ('to uncover nakedness' — the incest laws) [named-only]; the later exile sense is career color. Our 9:21 writes אָהֳלֹה ('his tent') with a final HEH where a vav is expected - verified in the ink at derivation - and the chain reads the feminine suffix as HER tent, making the exposure an offence against his wife's quarters. The reflexive uncovering-verb is read as bringing EXILE on himself and his descendants. And the number …

The seer is tagged AGAIN: Ham, FATHER OF CANAAN — the double tag's second half, the letter keeping the grandson in frame [letter fact; the chain's why is named-only].

(the garden's interrogation); token 2 = Ham telling his two brothers — outside [letter fact]. What the garden asked about, this verse performs [Onkelos sharpens the venue: ba-chutz ('outside') -> be-shuka ('in the MARKET') — the report made publicati…

WHAT WAS DONE IS DISPUTED, AND THE DISPUTE DECIDES THE CURSE'S TARGET [claim G23-12]. Rav and Shmuel divide: one holds he was castrated, the other sodomized - the castration reading argued from the MISSING FOURTH SON, the other by verbal analogy on the seeing-verb; the resolution offered is that all agree on castration and some add the second. VA-YIQACH — SINGULAR verb, TWO subjects: 'and-he-took, Shem and Yefet' [letter fact, held; the chain's credit-teaching is named-only; Onkelos KEEPS the singular — u-nesev]. SIMLAH ('garment') — Torah token 1 [Onkelos renders kesuta, 'the COVERING' — the garment named by its function; dual-track].

The set-verb (SUM, token 4): token 1 SET the man in the garden (2:8), token 2 SET the mark on Cain (4:15) — now it sets a garment on two shoulders [letter fact]. SHEKHEM ('shoulder') — Torah token 1 (rare: 7 tokens). The number flips to PLURAL here — one took, two carried [letter fact].
ACHORANNIT ('backward') — the word's ENTIRE Torah career is inside THIS VERSE: 2 tokens of 2, once for the feet, once for the faces [rare crown].

FROZEN PREDICTION LANDS #1: KASAH ('cover') token 3 — gen_18 logged at the verb's flood-debut (7:19-20, the waters covering the mountains, agentless passives): 'its next token covers a father's nakedness (9:23)' — and it does: the flood's burial verb turned filial, now with AGENTS and a garment [frozen-unit prediction landing].

The verse ends on the NOT-SEEING, held as fact: faces backward, 'and their father's nakedness they did NOT see' — the span's see-verb pair closing against 9:22's va-yar ('and he saw'): one saw and told; two covered and did not see [letter fact].

A RULING THAT TURNS ON THIS SUBJECT NOT BEING AN ISRAELITE [claim G23-14]. Rav Yehuda rules that a gentile's nakedness counts as nakedness for reciting the Shema, and his proof is this verse - 'their father's nakedness', said of a man who was not an Israelite. The operator's own subject is the argument. And from 'he SAW... and he TOLD' the organs of the offence are identified as the eye and the to…

YAQATZ ('awake') — Torah token 1 (rare: 5 tokens), and every LATER Torah awakening is from a dream of destiny (Jacob at Bethel, 28:16; Pharaoh x3, Gen 41); the first is from wine — MI-YENO, 'from his wine' [letter fact].

VA-YEDA ('and he KNEW') — the know-verb (token 10; Eden's tree-verb) aimed at a deed the letter NEVER STATES: what was done, and how he knew, are the chain's questions [OPEN, named-only]. BENO HA-QATAN ('his SMALL son') — QATAN token 2: token 1 was 1:16's LESSER light; the letter lists Ham second, the epithet says small — the tension is the letter's own [OPEN, held].

THE FIRST HUMAN CURSE-SPEECH — the delta from the precedents NAMED: the curse-ASSIGN device's earlier speakers were all DIVINE (3:14, 3:17, 4:11); here the curser is a man — and the man is the one whose own NAME was given against the curse (5:29: 'this one will comfort us … from the ground which YHWH cursed') [letter fact]. Noach's first quoted words in the corpus are this curse [letter fact].

Yudan states it outright: 'from here, a source from the Torah for TRANSLATIONS'. The reading then becomes law - the case-table's dispute over which languages a scro…

Held as FACT per gen_14's row class [decision recorded]; duration, not date — NO TIME_ANCHOR in this unit.
